column1: # mapping.tsv -- EmuTOS function -> NewTOS function (n:m) for every function
# defined in EmuTOS bios/ and bdos/ at the oracle pin (the `def` rows of
# edges.tsv). HAND-CURATED: each row is a reading of both sources; the
# EmuTOS side follows edges.tsv, so regenerate edges.tsv first, then fix
# One row per pair; several rows per EmuTOS function when NewTOS splits it.
#   design:<evidence>  no counterpart on purpose; newtos_file/newtos_fn `-`,
#                      the note says why. <evidence> is one of
#                        ADR-NNN@<file>:<line>  an ADR and where it stands:
#                        hardware:<device>  Atari hardware the Pi does not
#                        source:<path>      another named reason; <path> is a
#   unmapped           no counterpart yet, or none found; `-` `-` and a note.
# A function's class (per definition: fn + file) is unmapped if any of its
# rows is, else mapped if any row is, else design. EmuTOS functions of
# layers without rows here (vdi, aes, desk, include; ext = no def row) count
# as unmapped. `cargo xtask deps --coverage` gives the shares per layer;
# a `--up`/`--down` set is complete only if its touched layers hold no
# the EmuTOS function is a def row of emutos_file, the NewTOS file exists
# and has `fn <newtos_fn>`, every bios/ and bdos/ function has a row, the
# class is valid and agrees with the newtos columns, an ADR cite's line is
# in that ADR's section of the cited file, a source path exists.
